## Background

Literate programming connects explanations with code [@knuth1984].
@wickham2014 discusses how data structure can support analysis.
These citations describe the motivation; the measurements below are fictional.^[The
data is included only to demonstrate document features, not to support a scientific claim.]

## Method {#sec-method}

We compare three daily measurements before and after a hypothetical process change.
The mean is defined in @eq-mean.

$$
\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
$$ {#eq-mean}

## Results

| Day | Before | After |
|:----|-------:|------:|
| 1 | 12 | 10 |
| 2 | 15 | 12 |
| 3 | 9 | 8 |

: Fictional processing times in minutes. {#tbl-times}

Using the method in @sec-method, @tbl-times gives mean times of 12 and 10
minutes. This small fictional dataset is an illustration, not evidence of an effect.
